name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 motor-propelled up to 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and a motor of less than 750 watts (Idaho Code §49-106)
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph (Idaho Code §49-106)
Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, required since September 1, 2019 (Idaho Code §49-727)
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
Subject to the safety requirements of a bicycle, and its rider has a bicycle rider's rights and duties, including the duty of due care (Idaho Code §49-725, and §49-714 as amended by HB 500 (2026))
Like a bicycle, may treat a stop sign as a yield sign: slow down, yield, then proceed without stopping
On a sidewalk or crosswalk, the rider must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing

May be ridden wherever bicycles may, including multi-use paths, unless excluded by local ordinance or by signs the agency in charge posts after putting the exclusion on its board's agenda (Idaho Code §§49-725, 49-728)
Not subject to driver's license, title, registration, plate or financial responsibility requirements (Idaho Code §49-726)
A violation by its rider of the rules of the road is an infraction (Idaho Code §49-729)
